findings: No meaningful drift accumulation for this contractive damped plant (max diff 3e-17 vs peak 5.7e-5).
WAD-18 advantage here is bitwise reproducibility across build configurations, NOT accuracy; absolute 1e-18 quantization costs accuracy at small magnitudes.
Original claim 'eliminates 100% of floating-point drift' is NOT supported for this plant; narrowed to build-configuration reproducibility.
Untested: marginally stable, integrating, or chaotic plants where float error may accumulate; non-x86 float behavior.

plant: undamped, k=4, dt=2^-10 (exact in WAD/double/binary128), semi-implicit Euler, 2,000,000 cycles
findings: WAD-18 error is ~constant (~2e-15) across amplitude (absolute quantization); double error scales with amplitude (relative).
WAD-18 more accurate only for magnitudes ~>=0.1-1 (amp 1: ~9x on x, ~150x on energy); double wins by orders of magnitude at small amplitude.
Out-of-range (amp 4: k*x exceeds +-9.22) saturates and raises overflow flag: failure is loud, results invalid.
Accuracy advantage is regime-dependent; reproducibility advantage is regime-independent.
caveats: 8 sampled checkpoints, one trajectory per amplitude, one host
energy error is relative to reference semi-implicit-Euler energy, not the continuous energy

change: Reentrant API: wad_*_f / w128_*_f / r3_design_damper_f / r3_design_damper128_f take the overflow flag from the caller; global-flag functions are thin wrappers compiled out by -DWAD_NO_GLOBALS. r3.c no longer uses a static (target passed explicitly). Latent hazard fixed: target = w*4*1e18 is now computed as u128_mul64(w, 4e18) (the old w*4u could wrap in 64 bits for w >= 2^62).
evidence: regression: all pre-existing gates unchanged (trace hashes, oracles, sens results byte-identical)
-DWAD_NO_GLOBALS objects (wad18, wad128, r3, r3_128): nm shows no .data/.bss symbols

benchmark/reentrant_test.c in default and NO_GLOBALS builds: 8 threads x 3 rounds with per-thread flags equal the sequential reference; flag stays isolated to the overflowing thread; 14 deterministic flag unit cases; 6 new flag mutants killed (mutation gate now 18 mutants)

gate_time.cause: mutation gate ran every mutant against the full 12M-case test; killed mutants now stop at first mismatch (fail-fast). Survivors still run in full. Detection unchanged: 18/18 killed. nproc=1 on test host.

my_errors_this_step: mutation builds used -w (no warnings), which hid -Werror failures (unused parameter) in the real test builds until the gates ran; fixed
the wrapper-vs-_f comparison is nearly tautological (wrappers call _f); real evidence is the unchanged oracles/hashes plus the threaded and flag tests
verify time had crept to ~72 s, over the 60 s budget, before profiling
honest_limits: thread test shows no interference on one host; it is not a memory-model proof (the argument is that no mutable shared state exists, checked by symbol audit)
interrupt-safety and stack usage (r3 recursion depth <= ~60 frames) are not measured
default (global-flag) API is still not reentrant: claim N2 stays refuted for it
